newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

A squeeze on the expiry of the December futures contract pushed prices up to a $9 gain on the day shortly before the contract went off the board on Friday, trade sources said. Earlier the market had been balanced by commission house selling of December positions being met by light trade buying. March closed $1.30 lower at $302.10 while May lost 90 cents to close at $302.90.

In New York raw sugar futures settled near the day's lows in listless dealings. Front month March closed two points lower at 10.35 cents/lb, while May gave up one point to close at 10.48 cents/lb. Prices are generally expected to remain under pressure, given prospects of another surplus in 1996/97.

IRELAND - Sugar exports in June 1996 amounted to 5,088 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 6,081 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first three quarters of 1995/96 (October/June) up to 63,501 tonnes against 40,913 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 56,773 tonnes against 31,867 tonnes in 1993/94.

Major countries of destination in October/June 1995/96 were the United Kingdom with 33,584 tonnes whites against 31,675 tonnes and Israel with 11,226 tonnes, up from 5,612 tonnes. Sugar imports in October/June 1995/96 amounted to 6,079 tonnes against 7,924 tonnes in 1994/95. Total imports in 1994/95 reached 10,954 tonnes against 7,238 tonnes in 1993/94.

DENMARK - Sugar imports in August 1996 amounted to 3,738 tonnes raw value, which brought cumulative imports in the first eleven months of 1995/96 (October/August) up to 21,751 tonnes against 4,110 tonnes in the corresponding period the previous year. Major countries of origin in October/August 1995/96 were Germany with 14,283 tonnes whites against 3,030 tonnes and Sweden with 4,732 tonnes against 62 tonnes.

Sugar exports in August 1996 reached 24,434 tonnes, up from 16,594 tonnes exported in August 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/August 1995/96 up to 159,837 tonnes against 186,732 tonnes in October/August 1994/95. Total exports in 1994/95 amounted to 199,559 tonnes against 255,177 tonnes in 1993/94.
Major countries of destination in October/August 1995/96 were Norway with 106,619 tonnes whites against 103,690 tonnes and Sweden with 15,712 tonnes compared to 1,516 tonnes.

TURKEY - Results of Turkey's ninth beet test, carried out on October 15, showed an increase in sugar content to 16.3 per cent, up from 15.9 per cent at the end of September. Sugar yield per ha reached 8.530 tonnes, white value, up from 7.97 tonnes in the eighth test, while root weight reached 52.38 tonnes, up from 50.13 tonnes in the previous test.

Industry sources said that Turkey's state sugar factories company, Turkseker, is expected to produce 1.577 million tonnes, white value, in 1997/98, up from 1.475 million tonnes in 1996/97. The company runs 25 factories in Turkey and the figures do not include the output by three private factories.

EL SALVADOR - Sugar production in 1996/97 (November/October) is estimated at 349,600 tonnes, up from 309,515 tonnes produced in 1995/96 and 311,726 tonnes produced in 1994/95. Molasses production in 1996/97 is estimated at 28.4 million gallons, up from 26.4 million gallons last year and 32.441 million gallons in 1994/95. Industry sources have put sugar consumption in 1996/97 at 211,600 tonnes unchanged from the previous two years.

TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) has bought 13,000 tonnes of white sugar from Cargill Switzerland at $290 per tonne, official sources said. GEZA has cancelled the purchase of 13,000 tonnes of white sugar which was contained in the same tender announced on October 14, it was added.
